title: Evaluating Image Editing with LLMs: A Comprehensive Benchmark and Intermediate-Layer Probing Approach

key_facts.fact: TIEdit has 512 source images, eight editing tasks, ten editing models, and 5,120 edited images.
Twenty expert annotators produced 307,200 raw ratings, which were aggregated into 15,360 MOS values.
The three human-rating dimensions are perceptual quality, editing alignment, and content preservation; the overall MOS is their average.
Perceptual quality, editing alignment, content preservation, and overall score are modeled as four independent regression tasks and trained separately.
EditProbe uses InternVL3 as its MLLM backbone.

Stage 1 is an offline analysis on the frozen backbone that combines normalized KL divergence, layer discriminability ratio, and information entropy into a saliency score to select an intermediate layer.
Stage 2 averages the selected-layer final-token hidden states of the source-image and edited-image streams to form z(x).
The score head is a two-hidden-layer MLP with ReLU activations trained using MSE.
AdaLoRA modules are inserted into both the vision encoder and language model; only AdaLoRA parameters and the regression head are updated, while the original backbone stays frozen.
Training uses AdaLoRA rank 16, scale 32, dropout 0.05, 448×448 images, AdamW at 1e-5 with cosine decay and warm-up, batch size 8, and five epochs on a 40GB NVIDIA RTX A100.
